NOT TRUNCATED. Research ran 06:03-06:58 ET and closed with a RESEARCH COMPLETE block, so nothing was lost to the clock. All six captured candidates are published; none was dropped on arithmetic.

WHY FOUR OF SIX ARE POSITION MANAGEMENT AND ONLY ONE IS A NEW ENTRY. This is the honest skew and it is deliberate. IWM, TLT, XLU and OXY are updates to open positions, DKS is an exit, and CVS is the only new entry (itself an amendment to a 2026-11-05 order whose level has now been reached, not a second position). The day after a +7.0% Nasdaq squeeze driven by a personnel reversal, with a 95%-priced rate HIKE eleven sessions out and a core PCE print tomorrow at 08:30 ET, is not a day to add beta — it is a day to fix a book that is long defensives and duration into a hiking cycle. The report's own 11% hit rate across 47 closed trades is better explained by that one repeated bet than by 47 bad stock picks: 42 of the 47 were swing longs.

THE CENTRAL FACT. The Fed is ~95% priced to hike 25bp on 2026-12-09 (94% Kalshi/Polymarket, ~97% CME FedWatch, against 76.3% a month earlier), with a second January hike ~55-60% priced. Core PCE consensus RE-ACCELERATES to 3.2% y/y from 3.1%. The 10y is 4.92% against a 3.88% effective funds rate, so the real policy rate is only +0.68%. Monday's squeeze repriced one man's job title and repriced nothing about rates.

PRICES. Every equity and ETF figure here is the 2026-11-23 official close via finnhub, age ~861 minutes at synthesis. That is a CLOSED market ahead of a 09:30 ET open, not stale data. All six quotes re-fetched at synthesis and matched the research values exactly; all six ATR14 values independently re-fetched and matched.

SOURCES THAT FAILED, and what each cost:
- Every index quote (^GSPC, ^NDX, ^DJI, ^RUT, ^VIX), ES/NQ futures, DXY, gold and WTI returned ok:false — finnhub wants a CFD-index subscription, yahoo returned 429, stooq 404, no alphavantage key. ALL index context in this report is therefore ETF proxies (SPY/QQQ/IWM/GLD/USO/XLF/XHB), which are primary finnhub OHLCV. VIX, DXY, SPX and NDX are published as null rather than estimated.
- Options-implied move unavailable: market_data.py implied returned HTTP 401 from yahoo-options for both CVS and DKS, so the strategy's 'is the target inside what options price' check COULD NOT BE RUN on any candidate today. Every target here rests on price structure and ATR alone, which is a materially weaker basis than usual.
- Event-contract prices unavailable: Kalshi's public endpoints returned null yes_bid, yes_ask, last_price, volume and open_interest for every KXFEDDECISION, KXFED, KXCPIYOY and KXRATECUT market. Hence ZERO event-contract recommendations despite the strategy actively wanting them — a probability disagreement cannot be stated without the market's price, and no implied price was invented to make one work. The Fed odds quoted throughout come from news coverage of Kalshi/Polymarket/CME, not from a fetched quote.
- market_data.py events '<topic>' is not a real search — it pulls the first 200 open markets and substring-filters, so 'Fed' matched 'Federico Bondioli', a footballer. Series must be queried via ?series_ticker=. Worth fixing.
- Gold's absolute price levels and the forced-selling attribution come from market commentary sites, not primary data; WGC Q4 central-bank figures are not published yet. GLD's own OHLCV is primary.

ARITHMETIC, RECOMPUTED FROM SOURCE RATHER THAN CARRIED OVER. Every ratio was recomputed from the final entry, target and stop, and every stop re-measured in ATRs: IWM 2.27 at 2.07 ATR, TLT 2.67 at 1.93 ATR, XLU 2.20 at 2.29 ATR, CVS 2.00 at 2.02 ATR, OXY 2.08 at 2.03 ATR. All clear the 2.0 swing floor and all clear their asset-class stop floor (1.8 ATR ETF, 2.0 ATR stock). DKS carries no ratio by design — it is an exit, sized 0%.

RATIOS CLUSTERED NEAR THE FLOOR — stated because it is the signature CLAUDE.md warns about. CVS lands on exactly 2.00 and OXY on 2.08. The mitigating fact is that four of the five ratios belong to positions whose levels were set on earlier dates and are UNCHANGED today, so they were not fitted this morning; TLT at 1.93 ATR and CVS at 2.02 ATR are likewise inherited, not tuned. The one to treat with suspicion is CVS, the only new entry, at exactly 2.00 — and research said so itself, naming the 95.40 target as 'the weak part of this idea' because it requires recovering half a 30% de-rate in a swing horizon. A trim at sma20 86.30 is in the scale plan for that reason. No stop was tightened to improve any ratio, and three of the six actions explicitly forbid tightening.

OXY'S WIN PROBABILITY IS BELOW ITS OWN BREAK-EVEN, and it is published anyway as a HOLD rather than suppressed. Its 0.26 sits under the 0.325 implied by 1/(1+2.08), i.e. the position claims no edge. It clears both published floors from its fixed entry, and the decision on a filled position is hold-or-close rather than enter-or-not — research closed DKS on exactly this test and kept OXY only because sma20 at 57.95 sits above the 54.0 entry so a reachable target still yields positive reward. That is a thin distinction, it is stated as such, and the hold comes with a tightened invalidation: a daily close below the 52.55 ninety-day low exits ahead of the 50.15 stop. Flagged for the red team.

CONVICTION. All six scores are supported by the evidence as captured, checked against the kinds-plus-one rule: IWM 4 on 3 distinct kinds, TLT 3 on 3, XLU 3 on 2, CVS 3 on 2, DKS 3 on 2, OXY 2 on 1. None was inflated and none needed lowering. CVS's repetition is flagged honestly in its key_risk — four pitches in ten days is a flag, not conviction, and the CEO purchase is the only genuinely new fact since the first.

CORRELATION. Exactly at the cap, not over it. Three ideas depend on the Fed path into 2026-12-09 — IWM short, TLT, XLU — against a limit of 3. CVS is deliberately rate-insensitive, and DKS and OXY are risk reductions rather than bets.

LANES DELIBERATELY EMPTY. Nothing intraday: an intraday idea needs a same-session dated catalyst and today's only scheduled item is Conference Board confidence, while the real event is tomorrow at 08:30. No event contract: prices unfetchable, above. No futures: the /MNQ short was rejected because QQQ's 3.70% ATR demands a ~9.3% stop no reachable target repays. No long_term idea: market_data.py has no fundamentals or valuation command, so no bear case could be defended with a number, which is also why CVS is published as a swing rather than the long_term idea it might be. Not reached at all: small- and micro-cap screening, and crypto beyond the macro print. GLD was wanted and rejected in full on its arithmetic — the workings are on the watchlist rather than hidden.

HOLIDAY WEEK. Thursday 11/26 is closed and Friday 11/27 is a 13:00 ET half day; liquidity drains from Wednesday afternoon, which exaggerates any PCE surprise. That is why the IWM stop was left wide at 284.5 rather than pulled in, and why the DKS exit carries a 11/27 time stop.

WHAT THE MECHANICAL VALIDATOR FLAGGED, AND WHY TWO FAILURES ARE LEFT STANDING RATHER THAN FIXED. Every reward-to-risk ratio was recomputed independently by validate_report.py against live prices and matched the figure published here exactly, in all five cases that have one (2.27, 2.67, 2.20, 2.00, 2.08 — claimed equals computed). Four ideas warn and two fail.

The warnings are mostly one thing worth knowing: IWM at 2.07 ATR, TLT at 1.93 ATR, CVS at 2.02 ATR and OXY at 2.03 ATR all clear their published floors but sit UNDER the 2.25-2.5 ATR band where this report's historical stop-outs have clustered. Four of the five are inherited levels on filled positions that cannot now be widened without moving a stop on a live trade, so the warning is recorded rather than engineered away. The others are benign: no bid/ask outside regular hours, and no datetime on the three ideas whose catalyst is genuinely undated.

OXY fails on expectancy — 26% claimed against a 32% break-even at 2.08:1, an expectancy of -0.20R, i.e. the idea loses money at its own stated hit rate. This is left exactly as it is. Raising win_probability to 0.33 would clear the check and would be precisely the fitting-numbers-to-pass failure the 2b-2d phases exist to catch; the 0.26 is research's own derivation and it stands. If phase 2d demotes OXY to the watchlist, that is the floor working as designed, and the position-management guidance still holds: do not add, and a daily close below the 52.55 ninety-day low exits ahead of the 50.15 stop.

DKS fails for a structural reason rather than a substantive one, and the distinction matters: it is a CLOSE instruction being measured by a validator built for entries. 'No stop, so risk is undefined' and 'no entry or stop, so the stop distance is undefined' are both true and both inapplicable — a position being sold has no stop, and inventing one to pass would be fabricating a risk control on a trade being exited. Its third failure, a 10.53% bid/ask spread costing '301% of the target move', is an off-hours quote artifact on a $133 stock, not a real spread; the validator itself notes elsewhere that no bid/ask is available outside regular hours. The exit case rests on the arithmetic in the thesis — 9:1 against from spot, a 0.70 ATR remaining stop, and three repair routes each failing a published floor — not on clearing an entry screen. Should enforcement demote it, read the watchlist entry as the live instruction: sell the shares into the 131.0-136.4 band, do not establish a short.

RED TEAM (phase 2c). Six ideas in, three out. Cut CVS, DKS and OXY; downgraded IWM from 4 to 3; re-ranked the three survivors; corrected one figure in the notes above.

CVS IS THE ONLY DISCRETIONARY KILL, and the reason is arithmetic rather than judgement. Its 95.40 target is exactly what the 2.0 floor requires from the published levels — 79.80 + 2 x (79.80 - 72.00) = 95.4000, matching the published number to the cent — and it is the only one of the five targets for which that is true; IWM, TLT, XLU and OXY all sit away from their floor-implied figures (242.50, 83.30, 46.30, 61.70). Nothing in the 1-year 58.50-110.68 range marks 95.40 and no evidence entry cites a level there. The nearest defensible resistance above is sma50 88.11, which yields 1.07:1, and the sma20 86.30 the thesis itself calls 'reachable' yields 0.83:1 — both under the floor — and the stop cannot repair them, since 72.00 is already 2.02 ATR against a 2.0 ATR stock floor. The amendment had also walked the stop IN, from the 2026-11-05 order's 71.50 (2.20 ATR) to 72.00 (2.02 ATR), so both legs of the level set moved toward the minimum that passes. Synthesis named the target 'the weak part of this idea' and was right: an idea that clears the floor only at a price no structure supports never cleared it. The order was still pending, so this abandons no live position.

DKS AND OXY WERE ALREADY FAILING THE MECHANICAL CHECKS and phase 2d would have demoted both. Doing it here buys two things. First a usable instruction: enforcement's note would have read 'no stop, so risk is undefined', which is true of every exit and tells the holder of a live DKS long nothing. Second, and more important, DKS carried direction 'sell' while the open DKS row is direction 'buy', and merge_report keys a position on (symbol, direction) — so a DKS 'sell' surviving into publish would have opened a NEW short at 133.67 rather than closing the 144.50 long, the exact thing the recommendation's own condition forbids. Demotion prevents that by design instead of by luck. Both watchlist notes carry the operative instruction, because the live positions stay tracked on their stored levels whether or not anyone acts.

OXY'S KILL IS ON ITS OWN STATED NUMBERS: 0.26 against a 0.325 break-even is -0.20R, the thesis is being falsified rather than merely unconfirmed (crude made a lower low on the single biggest risk-on day since April 2025, and XLE was the only red sector ETF), spot is 0.3% above the 90-day low, and conviction 2 rests on one evidence kind. Synthesis declined to raise win_probability to make it pass; that was the right call, and this demotion is its consequence rather than a rebuke.

WHERE THE REPORT HAS TWO IDEAS BACKWARDS. It closes DKS on an enter-or-not test while holding OXY on a hold-or-close test, and the choice of frame is what produces the opposite verdicts, not the underlying facts — applied consistently from spot the two look alike (DKS 1.89:1 to sma20 142.48, OXY 2.06:1 to sma20 57.95). What actually separates them is evidence: DKS's seven-insider, $5.59M cluster bracketing spot on the window's heaviest up-volume is intact, while OXY's crude thesis is being contradicted by new data. On thesis grounds the weaker hold is OXY. The DKS exit is left standing anyway, because its published 175.50 target is genuinely unreachable in a swing horizon, so the position as published cannot win and something had to change. Its exit instruction is also corrected from the market order it was published as to a limit, which the validator asked for on a 1.74% spread, and the watchlist note carries it.

ONE FIGURE ABOVE IS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED RATHER THAN EDITED AWAY: the DKS spread is 1.74%, costing 50% of the target move, per its validation block. The 10.53% spread 'costing 301% of the target move' quoted earlier is a pre-revalidation figure, and the argument it was making — that an off-hours spread on a $133 stock is an artifact — survives at the smaller number.

IWM GOES TO CONVICTION 3 because its central mechanism is measurably not working. The claim is that the most floating-rate-levered index underperforms into a hiking path; over the month in which hike odds went from 76.3% to 95% — the cleanest test the thesis will ever get — IWM OUTPERFORMED SPY by 1.33%, which the report concedes in its own counter_argument. Its dated_catalyst is a 25bp hike priced at 94-97%, which is agreement with the market rather than a disagreement with it, and no reason is given why the path should reprice further. The position is kept, since it is the only thing in the book aligned with the rate regime and carries the best expectancy here at +0.37R, but 4 claimed an edge the evidence does not pay for.

NOTHING WAS CUT FOR CORRELATION, AND THE CAP WAS NOT THE BINDING CONSTRAINT IT WAS DESCRIBED AS. 'Three ideas depend on the Fed path' counts IWM, TLT and XLU together, but IWM short needs rates higher while TLT and XLU need them lower, so this is not one position wearing three tickers — it is a 2-vs-1 straddle of the same axis. Worth saying plainly: after the cuts the entire report is three ETFs at 2% each expressing a rate view in both directions, which means the honest read of today is that the book has no net conviction, not that it has three.

RE-RANKED ON STRUCTURE RATHER THAN RATIO. IWM 1 (only regime-aligned position, best expectancy at +0.37R). XLU 2 (the only idea in the report whose stop clears the 2.25 ATR guide outright, the lowest ATR in the book at 1.51%, above its 50-day, and a target at a real range high). TLT 3 (the highest ratio at 2.67 but the least believed — its 84.30 target sits at the top of the 90-day range and is reachable mainly if the ~95%-priced hike path the rest of the report rests on fails, so that ratio is conditional on the central thesis being wrong; its counter_argument now says so).

XLU'S LEVELS AND CONVICTION STAND BUT ITS CATALYST IS RESTATED. 'Datacenter power demand re-ignited' rests on an NVIDIA press release about NVIDIA's CEO, three inferential steps from utility load growth, with no utility-specific datum behind it, and on the day the catalyst supposedly fired XLU added 1.48% — about one ATR, off a 42.63 low, on the biggest risk-on day in 19 months — which is indistinguishable from beta. XLU is also down from 44.12 on 11/16, so it is rolling over rather than breaking out. Conviction 3 is retained on the structural leg alone, not because the narrative leg was answered.

LEVELS RE-VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY, and the report's price discipline is not the problem anywhere — only its level selection, in exactly one place. Every technical_level figure re-fetched and matched to the decimal: XLU 43.32 / sma20 43.417 / sma50 41.971 / 90d 39.03-46.625; IWM 265.74 / sma20 275.6625 / sma50 277.8202 / 90d low 256.32 / -12.92% off high; CVS 79.65 / sma20 86.296 / sma50 88.1122 / 90d low 77.33 / -28.04%; OXY 52.70 / 90d low 52.55 / sma20 57.946 / ATR 1.8938. IWM's target also survives the test that killed CVS's: 238.69 sits below the 90-day low of 256.32 and so is in open space on that window, but it is inside the 1-year 206.81-305.18 range and it is not the floor-implied 242.50, so it was chosen rather than fitted.

market_context.summary: A two-day event dominates the tape: Friday 11/20 was a correlation-to-one liquidation — stocks, gold AND crypto fell together while Treasuries rallied, on multiples of normal volume — and Monday 11/23 snapped back +4.71% on SPY and +7.00% on QQQ after Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang, with Trump saying he personally intervened. NVDA closed +31%, the best Nasdaq session since 2025-04-09. But the snapback closed weak: SPY finished 722.29 below its 724.33 open, QQQ mid-range off its high, and EVERYTHING remains below both its 20- and 50-day. The central fact is unchanged by any of it: the Fed is ~95% priced to HIKE 25bp on 2026-12-09, a second January hike is ~55-60% priced, and core PCE consensus re-accelerates to 3.2% y/y at tomorrow's 08:30 ET print. Crude diverged — USO fell 4.49% to a lower low on the biggest risk-on day in 19 months — which says this inflation is services, shelter and goods rather than energy-led, i.e. the stickier kind a Fed cannot wait out. ATRs are enormous (QQQ 3.70%, IWM 2.54%), so a 2.0 ATR swing stop on QQQ is 7.4%. Gold is the biggest dislocation on the board at 22.45% off its 90-day high, and it was rejected as a long on its own arithmetic rather than its story. Thanksgiving Thursday is closed and Friday is a half day, so liquidity thins from Wednesday afternoon and any PCE surprise moves more than it should.
